principle: Where Rafter demonstrably leads, where evidence is mixed, and what remains unmeasured.

completion_boundaries: proposal submitted -> reference application operation completes on leader
sections.conditions: Three voters in one process, in-memory stores, no disk synchronization or TCP. Workloads use submission bursts, not a continuously replenished concurrency window.
details: All adapters execute the same leader-side reference application operation; 7 repetitions.
Selected identities: rafter 3f2cdc956eaa; raft-rs 0.7.0 (crate `raft`, prost-codec); openraft 0.9.24 (features: storage-v2; current-thread tokio).
sections.question: How quickly can the implementation replicate and commit without disks or sockets?
sections.result: Rafter leads 12 of 12 qualified throughput and p99 comparisons with no measured regressions.
sections.title: Consensus in memory

sections.conditions: One identical Rafter binary, 256-byte proposals, three repetitions; batch size is explicit in every row. Selected Rafter revision: 8b3f7e71cb23.
sections.question: How efficiently does Rafter make consensus state survive a restart?
sections.result: The append-only journal improved throughput 45.3–61.4% over Rafter's file-replacement backend.

journal.scope: fixed hard-state syscall probe; not synchronization calls per committed entry

replace.scope: fixed hard-state syscall probe; not synchronization calls per committed entry

sections.title: Durable replication

objective.evaluation: Every repetition must meet the rate and tail limits; accounting is summed without survivor filtering.

capacity.result: At 0 ms added egress, Rafter met the declared service objective through at least 1,000 writes/s; the selected OpenRaft control met it through at least 1,000 writes/s.

sections.conditions: three processes on one host; real TCP, not three physical hosts; 64 clients; 512-byte writes; medians of 3 repetitions. Success requires Raft commitment and durable application completion. Added delay affects client and peer egress. Storage, codec, and scheduling choices differ between integrations. Selected identities: Rafter 8b3f7e71cb23; OpenRaft synchronous 0.9.24.
sections.question: How many durable writes can an application complete, and how long do clients wait?
sections.result: Rafter pipeline + completion priority completed 3.52× as many durable writes per second as the tested OpenRaft synchronous integration in the no-delay condition.
sections.title: Complete durable service

checks.scope: finite histories and canaries, not every measured write or power loss

checks.name: Rafter recovery smoke
checks.scope: smoke correctness only; not comparative performance

sections.question: Does performance remain useful during failures and over long runs?
sections.result: Finite recovery checks passed; comparative fault and sustained-operation performance remain unmeasured.
